landmarks.name: Geghard Monastery
landmarks.writeup: A UNESCO World Heritage site, partially carved out of the adjacent mountain, known for its medieval Armenian architecture.

landmarks.name: Garni Temple
landmarks.writeup: A first-century pagan temple, the only Greco-Roman colonnaded building in the former Soviet Union.

landmarks.name: Khor Virap Monastery
landmarks.writeup: Famous for its location near Mount Ararat and its historical significance in Armenian Christianity.

landmarks.name: Republic Square
landmarks.writeup: The central town square in Yerevan, known for its distinctive Soviet-era architecture and musical fountains.

landmarks.name: Lake Sevan
landmarks.writeup: One of the largest freshwater high-altitude lakes in the world, popular for recreation and natural beauty.

cultural_events.name: Vardavar
cultural_events.writeup: An ancient Armenian festival where people splash water on each other, celebrated in summer with roots in pagan traditions.

cultural_events.name: Armenian Genocide Remembrance Day
cultural_events.writeup: Observed on April 24 to commemorate the victims of the 1915 Armenian Genocide.

cultural_events.name: Yerevan Wine Days
cultural_events.writeup: An annual festival celebrating Armenia's ancient winemaking heritage with tastings and cultural events.

food_writeup: Armenian cuisine features rich flavors with staples like lavash bread, khorovats (barbecue), dolma (stuffed grape leaves), and a variety of fresh herbs, nuts, and dried fruits reflecting its agricultural heritage.
brief_history: Armenia is one of the world's oldest civilizations, first adopting Christianity as a state religion in 301 AD. It has a rich history marked by periods of independence and foreign domination, including Persian, Ottoman, and Soviet rule, regaining independence in 1991.
current_conflicts: Ongoing tensions and periodic clashes with Azerbaijan over the Nagorno-Karabakh region remain a significant security issue.
